top.title: Former Rice football coach and player Ray Alborn dies at age 87
top.description: Rice coach Ray Alborn is carried off the field after the Owls beat UH in 1980. (Sam C. Pierson Jr./Houston Chronicle) Former Rice football coach Ray Alborn, who also played for the Owls, died on Thursday, the school announced. He was 87. Alborn coached the Owls from 1978-83. His best season was in 1980 when Rice went 5-6 with wins over LSU, TCU, Texas A&M, Arkansas and Houston. Overall, he was 13-53 on South Main. Alborn, who played in high school at Houston Lamar, signed to play with Rice in 1957. His junior season, Alborn was a starter at defensive tackle and helped the Owls to the Sugar Bowl. He was a team captain as a senior. Alborn started his coaching career at junior highs in the Houston area before becoming head coach at Sharpstown in 1969. He returned to Rice in 1972 as a defensive line coach on Al Conover's staff. He was defensive coordinator for Homer Rice. After Rice, Alborn coached the defensive tackles for Jack Pardee with the Houston Gamblers of the USFL. He coached Lamar University from 1986-89 and was 13-30 overall, including 5-5 in 1989 before the school opted to drop football. Alborn returned to coaching in 1998 at Lamar Consolidated. He led the Mustangs to their first winning season in 18 years in 1999 and a spot in the playoffs. A visitation will be held from 6-8 p.m. on Wednesday in Sugar Land at Settegast-Kopf Co. at 15015 Southwest Freeway. A memorial service will be at 11 a.m. on Thursday at Sugar Land Methodist Church at 431 Eldridge Road. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. top.title: Sewickley Academy captures fifth WPIAL girls soccer title in program history
top.description: PITTSBURGH — When top-seeded Sewickley Academy hit the pitch for the WPIAL Class 1A girls high school soccer championship match against No. 2 Winchester, it lost just one match since its defeat in last year’s finals, falling in the quarterfinals of the PIAA playoffs. That impressive streak continued Friday, November 6 at F.N.B. Stadium as Sewickley Academy knocked off Winchester Thurston 2-0 to claim its fifth WPIAL championship in program history and its first title since 2004. “When I was a freshman, winning a playoff game, let alone playing and winning a WPIAL championship, was something that I did not think was possible,” senior forward Emma Eannarino said. “To be here and put together the year that we’ve had, it has shown how much we have grown as a group and how hard we work for everything.” Last season in the title game, Sewickley Academy (19-0-0) was shut out by Bentworth and fell in heartbreaking fashion, after surrendering a late goal. But in this year’s match, Sewickley Academy was the aggressor from the jump and was backed by a stellar back line. The Panthers wasted little time to get on the board, with Sewickley Academy taking the early lead after midfielder Claire Karsman crossed a ball inside the box and was finished off by fellow sophomore striker Sarah Merryman. “We talked heading into this about getting that first goal on the board,” Sewickley Academy head coach Gary Weber said. “Our back line has been solid all year and the backs have been spectacular.” Required Reading: WPIAL high school football playoffs Beaver Valley live score updates Required Reading: Beaver Valley teams gear up for WPIAL high school soccer championships Required Reading: OLSH girls high school volleyball eyeing first WPIAL championship After recording an assist in the match’s first goal, Karsman put up a crucial insurance tally in the 59th minute, manoeuvring her way inside the box and putting it past the Winchester Thurston (18-3-0) goalkeeper into the top left corner of the net. “I was getting pushed around down in the box but saved the ball from going out,” Karsman said. “Once I turned, I saw the goal and just shot it. The girl in front of her, Lila Peluso, is also a freshman and has stepped up well after our starting defender went out with a concussion earlier.” With the win, Sewickley Academy will now set its sights on the PIAA playoffs, as it will take on the runner-up of District V at a site and time to be determined on Tuesday, November 10. How much of an impact will the acquisition of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner have on the 49ers? Where would you rank this in the pantheon of their midseason trades in recent years? Eric Branch: It obviously ranks below the 2022 Christian McCaffrey blockbuster on the deadline Richter scale and it's not quite on par with the 2019 Emmanuel Sanders deal. top.title: Shenendehowa girls' volleyball continues Section 2 title streak
top.description: Shenendehowa celebrates after beating Saratoga in the Section 2, Class AAA finals on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - The Shenendehowa girls' volleyball team boasts a powerhouse up front, with several weapons the Mustangs can call on to make an impact. In Friday's Section 2 Class AAA championship, Shenendehowa's potent offense was the focus once again as the top-seeded Mustangs swept past No. 2 Saratoga Springs in straight sets 25-13, 25-14, 25-16, at Saratoga Springs High School. "It makes it so fun because the defense doesn't really have one person to focus on," Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. "They have to focus on three hitting options at all times, and running a 6-2 with two great setters, they're spreading it out. It's such a great part of our offense." Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped in five kills. Shenendehowa, the top-ranked team in the state Class AAA poll, pushed its sectional title win streak to six with. The four most recent championships have come in Class AAA since the state expanded to a six-classification system. "It's a completely new team than what we've had in the past," Ennist said. "It's a ton of younger girls and some seniors. It's just such a big mix and honestly, we're doing a great job together. It's so fun to be able to play with such a variety of ages and abilities out there." Key moment Shenendehowa trailed 6-5 in the second set, but used a pair of runs to gain control. The Mustangs used a 7-0 spurt to grab a 12-6 lead, and Ennist set up sophomore Leah Alfandre for a kill to cap a 5-1 run which provided Shenendehowa its first double-digit lead of the set, 17-7. "Those were really big for us, especially in a game this competitive," Ennist said. "If you do get into a little bit of a rut, you still have so much time to come out of it, and I think we did a really great job of getting that lead." Star of the game Shenendehowa freshman setter Kyli Kessler, the coach's daughter, turned in a stellar all-around performance. Kessler finished with 19 assists, 12 service points, including a pair of aces, and nine digs. "She works hard year-round on her game," Lori Kessler said of her daughter. "I think that she really wanted to prove herself this season, and I think that her being surrounded by the girls, by the great passing and the great hitters, makes her job a little bit easier for her. But regardless, she's still an everyday hard worker that if something feels off, she's the first one out there that wants to fix it and make it better for everybody." top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Clark has had plenty to say about how his time at ESPN came to an end. The former NFL analyst was laid off in July, and he found out while he was still on the air. Now, Clark is suggesting that the way it all played out was planned. Clark has previously made it clear that he believes ESPN wanted his firing to become a story. Now, he’s arguing that it used an interview with Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham to show it was changing direction. Clark’s ESPN exit Clark was pulled off the set of NFL Live in the middle of the show on July 20. ESPN had planned to tell him the next day as part of a wider round of layoffs, but word of his departure got out first. OutKick, the conservative-leaning outlet owned by Fox that had long been critical of Clark, had the story before it was published elsewhere. OutKick’s Bobby Burack said that the outlet gave ESPN an hour’s notice so the network could tell Clark itself, according to Awful Announcing . ESPN then moved to tell Clark before he could find out on social media. A day later, ESPN published a profile of Cunningham , in which the Indiana Fever guard said she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls’ and women’s sports. “I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men,” Cunningham told ESPN. Cunningham also said she had received “a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans,” adding, “I never once said that.” The comments made her one of the biggest stories in the WNBA, and she has since insisted her political views are “right in the middle.” Clark has already called his firing “purposeful,” saying on The Breakfast Club earlier this fall that ESPN handled it in a way that was meant to humiliate him. ‘That’s what they wanted’ On Thursday, Clark took things a step further during an appearance on All The Smoke . top.description: Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) is out on a batted ball during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power , but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees’ second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability. A Fresh Start in Washington The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm’s move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams. The Reds Need an Offensive Boost With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league’s lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm’s two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona’s order. The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. top.title: NASCAR Confirms Major Qualifying Change for 2027, With More Changes on the Table
top.description: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 31: Denny Hamlin, driver of the #11 King's Hawaiian Maple Brown Sugar Toyota, climbs into his car during qualifying for the NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway on October 31, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images) Getty NASCAR is making a significant change to how starting lineups are determined in 2027, and that might not be the only qualifying shakeup coming next season. John Probst, NASCAR’s president of event management, confirmed Friday, Nov. 6, that the sanctioning body will abandon its current qualifying metric when weather or other circumstances prevent a qualifying session from taking place. Beginning in 2027, starting lineups for those races will instead be determined strictly by owner points. The announcement comes during championship weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway, just hours after NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell acknowledged concerns about the existing system during his annual State of the Sport address. And while the new procedure for canceled qualifying sessions is confirmed, NASCAR is also exploring two other possibilities: eliminating the second round of superspeedway qualifying and introducing pit stops into qualifying at select races. NASCAR Is Changing How Starting Lineups Are Set in 2027 For years, NASCAR has relied on a formula to determine starting lineups whenever qualifying cannot be completed. That formula considers several factors, including previous race results and owner points, rather than simply awarding starting positions based on the championship standings. The system has occasionally produced starting grids that look considerably different from the current points order, particularly early in the season when teams have fewer races behind them. That has raised questions about fairness, especially when multiple qualifying sessions are canceled during the opening weeks of a season. Speaking Friday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio, Probst confirmed that NASCAR will move away from the formula in 2027. #NASCAR ’s John Probst tells @SiriusXMNASCAR that starting lineups for rained out qualifying sessions will be set by Owner’s Points in 2027. Probst also mentions that NASCAR is looking at an All-Star-like qualifying format for some races in 2027 (with a pit stop in the middle).… — Joseph Srigley (@joe_srigley) November 6, 2026 Under the new procedure, owner points alone will determine starting positions when qualifying is canceled. It’s a straightforward adjustment, but one that could have meaningful consequences for teams. A strong position in the owner standings would carry an additional benefit on weekends when drivers never get the opportunity to qualify. The change also removes the influence of individual race results from the canceled-qualifying calculation. Importantly, this applies to races where qualifying cannot be held. top.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (photos)
top.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

top.title: Ben James produces another low round and takes the 36-hole lead in Mexico
top.description: CABO SAN LUCAS, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 06: Ben James of the United States plays his shot from the fourth tee during the second round of the World Wide Technology Championship 2026 at El Cardonal at Diamante on November 06, 2026 in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images LOS CABOS, Mexico — Ben James ran off five straight birdies around the turn and finished with an aggressive tee shot for one last birdie and an 8-under 64 on Friday to build a one-shot lead going into the weekend at the World Wide Technology Championship. James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer. He already has four finishes in the top 5 and picking up plenty of experience along the way. A victory would put him on the Championship Series under the new model in 2028 and move him into the top 50 in the world. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” James was at 15-under 129 at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal at Diamante. He was one shot ahead of Peter Malnati, who was tied for the lead until coming up short of the green on the par-3 ninth and missing a 12-foot par putt to end his round of 64. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where ... I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair had a 68 and was three shots behind. This is the second time James has had the lead going into the weekend. The other was the RBC Canadian Open, and he shot a 78 to quickly spiral out of contention. He also had a good chance to win the Biltmore Championship Asheville until Jacob Bridgeman put on a putting clinic down the stretch in the final round. “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” He won the par-5 18th when he least expected it. James has been relying on his short wedges, and hit a pedestrian pitch to about 18 feet. But he holed the putt, and then started the front nine with three straight birdies to set the target. top.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. nigeria.title: The Obidient Pulse: Obi Warns Against Uncertainty As Opposition Groups Face A Test Of Unity

Obi reacts to court ruling affecting ADC The Federal High Court in Abuja has nullified the leadership of the African Democratic Congress under Senator David Mark and set aside the party’s processes, including the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate. The ADC says it will appeal. Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, described the ruling as “unsettling and surprising”. He said there should be certainty about parties and candidates ahead of an election and called for opposition politics to be protected. Obi also accused the ruling APC of engineering the instability, an allegation the party rejected. The court decision concerns the ADC; it does not directly affect Obi’s NDC candidacy. Court fight places opposition unity under pressure The ADC has rejected the judgment and says it will challenge it in court. Atiku has also said he will appeal and seek a stay of execution. The case now puts the spotlight on the judiciary’s role in resolving internal party disputes and on whether opposition parties can maintain stable platforms as the election approaches. Disagreement among Obi’s support groups continues The court ruling comes amid public friction between the OK Movement and leaders of the Obidient Movement and NDC campaign. The OK Movement accused them of fuelling divisions; the NDC campaign dismissed the dispute as a distraction, while the Obidient coordinator’s aide said he was focused on mobilising support for Obi. The exchanges raise a practical question for the campaign: can its different support groups coordinate their work, clarify who speaks for whom and build lasting grassroots organisation? The public disagreements are a reminder that a broad support base needs clear roles and disciplined coordination to turn enthusiasm into effective political mobilisation. The task ahead For the Obidient Movement, the immediate challenge is to keep attention on voters, organisation and the issues facing Nigerians. The movement’s strength will be measured not only by the size of its support, but by how effectively it organises that support across communities and sustains a credible campaign. In a political season increasingly shaped by court cases and internal disputes, the demand from supporters is likely to be simple: less public quarrelling, clearer communication and visible work on the ground. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. business.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . business.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Former Rice football coach and player Ray Alborn dies at age 87
sports.description: Rice coach Ray Alborn is carried off the field after the Owls beat UH in 1980. (Sam C. Pierson Jr./Houston Chronicle) Former Rice football coach Ray Alborn, who also played for the Owls, died on Thursday, the school announced. He was 87. Alborn coached the Owls from 1978-83. His best season was in 1980 when Rice went 5-6 with wins over LSU, TCU, Texas A&M, Arkansas and Houston. Overall, he was 13-53 on South Main. Alborn, who played in high school at Houston Lamar, signed to play with Rice in 1957. His junior season, Alborn was a starter at defensive tackle and helped the Owls to the Sugar Bowl. He was a team captain as a senior. Alborn started his coaching career at junior highs in the Houston area before becoming head coach at Sharpstown in 1969. He returned to Rice in 1972 as a defensive line coach on Al Conover's staff. He was defensive coordinator for Homer Rice. After Rice, Alborn coached the defensive tackles for Jack Pardee with the Houston Gamblers of the USFL. He coached Lamar University from 1986-89 and was 13-30 overall, including 5-5 in 1989 before the school opted to drop football. Alborn returned to coaching in 1998 at Lamar Consolidated. He led the Mustangs to their first winning season in 18 years in 1999 and a spot in the playoffs. sports.title: NASCAR Confirms Major Qualifying Change for 2027, With More Changes on the Table
sports.description: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 31: Denny Hamlin, driver of the #11 King's Hawaiian Maple Brown Sugar Toyota, climbs into his car during qualifying for the NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway on October 31, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images) Getty NASCAR is making a significant change to how starting lineups are determined in 2027, and that might not be the only qualifying shakeup coming next season. John Probst, NASCAR’s president of event management, confirmed Friday, Nov. 6, that the sanctioning body will abandon its current qualifying metric when weather or other circumstances prevent a qualifying session from taking place. Beginning in 2027, starting lineups for those races will instead be determined strictly by owner points. The announcement comes during championship weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway, just hours after NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell acknowledged concerns about the existing system during his annual State of the Sport address. And while the new procedure for canceled qualifying sessions is confirmed, NASCAR is also exploring two other possibilities: eliminating the second round of superspeedway qualifying and introducing pit stops into qualifying at select races. NASCAR Is Changing How Starting Lineups Are Set in 2027 For years, NASCAR has relied on a formula to determine starting lineups whenever qualifying cannot be completed. That formula considers several factors, including previous race results and owner points, rather than simply awarding starting positions based on the championship standings. The system has occasionally produced starting grids that look considerably different from the current points order, particularly early in the season when teams have fewer races behind them. That has raised questions about fairness, especially when multiple qualifying sessions are canceled during the opening weeks of a season. Speaking Friday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio, Probst confirmed that NASCAR will move away from the formula in 2027. #NASCAR ’s John Probst tells @SiriusXMNASCAR that starting lineups for rained out qualifying sessions will be set by Owner’s Points in 2027. Probst also mentions that NASCAR is looking at an All-Star-like qualifying format for some races in 2027 (with a pit stop in the middle).… — Joseph Srigley (@joe_srigley) November 6, 2026 Under the new procedure, owner points alone will determine starting positions when qualifying is canceled. It’s a straightforward adjustment, but one that could have meaningful consequences for teams. A strong position in the owner standings would carry an additional benefit on weekends when drivers never get the opportunity to qualify. The change also removes the influence of individual race results from the canceled-qualifying calculation. Importantly, this applies to races where qualifying cannot be held. sports.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. The team must play a game–a pretty important game, really, as all these games are now made much more important thanks to recent failures–against the Colts on the road and, in doing so, they will see what a team in the midst of a massive sell looks like. The Colts have dumped stars in the past 10 days, and could dump at least one more if running back Jonathan Taylor is sent out by Tuesday. Might playing against a team in the throws of an on-the-fly rebuild inspire team owner Jerry Jones to shift his thinking and rebuild his spent draft capital? There has been ample conversation about trading away George Pickens, but that has apparently been more smoke than fire. But whether things could change was the question put to Jones on Friday afternoon during a radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, and the owner was clear in his stance. That’s because Chimaev was expected to handle Strickland in dominant fashion and start a 185-pound title reign that we haven’t seen since Israel Adesanya. technology.title: Man unexpectedly recovers from a knife wound through his eye and brain
technology.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region. Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. technology.title: PyTorch 2.15 tackles the 'one bad GPU' problem
technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. science.title: Hera probe gets 1st good look at asteroid system clobbered by NASA's DART mission | Space photo of the day for Nov. 6, 2026
science.description: null The Didymos binary asteroid system, as seen by Europe's Hera probe. The main asteroid, Didymos, dominates the frame while just a sliver of its "moonlet," Dimorphos, is visible beneath it. ESA released this image on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: ESA) The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid system. If that system sounds familiar, it's because it made headlines in September 2022 when NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft smashed into it. The aim of the DART mission was to test whether an impact could divert an asteroid away from a collision course with Earth. The purpose of Hera is to follow up on DART by making up-close observations of the Didymos system. "The first thing we said was, 'Wow,'" Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel said in a statement about the image, which ESA released on Thursday (Nov. 5). "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART’s camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole new world." What is it? The Didymos system consists of the eponymous 2,560-foot-wide (780 meters) space rock and its "moonlet" Dimorphos, which is about 530 feet (160 m) in diameter. The DART mission impacted Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022, with the aim of causing a change in the orbital period of the moonlet. And it worked: Before the impact, Dimorphos completed one lap around Didymos in around 11 hours and 55 minutes. The DART collision reduced the length of this period by around 33 minutes. The change is a result of the fact that Dimporphos is now traveling at around 2.7 millimeters per second more slowly than it did before the collision. The newly released photo shows Didymos in detail. Just a sliver of Dimorphos is visible, below and slightly to the left of the main asteroid. Why is it incredible? The changes caused by DART were small. But in a real Earth-threatening scenario, even such a tiny shift could help divert an asteroid on a collision course — as long as scientists get enough advance warning of its approach. Hera's observations should help reveal what other changes have occurred on and around Didymos. Scientists are already seeing that, while Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator as before the impact, many changes have occurred. This includes the creation of multiple boulders, craters, and patterns of grooves or ridges. "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 kilometer [0.62 miles] of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out," said Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist. "We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify." Stay tuned to Space.com for more Hera findings from Didymos.
